```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(cluster)  # for silhouette()

options(bdat602.source_only = TRUE)
source("courses/bdat-602/_teacher/resources/datasets/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
# Use 50,000 rows for speed
health_data <- simulate_bdat602(n = 50000, seed = 602)
```

## Task 1: Prepare and scale clustering features

```{r task1-prepare}
# TODO: select age, bmi, income, num_claims, num_chronic_conditions
# Drop rows with any NA, then scale() all columns
clust_data <- health_data |>
  select(age, bmi, income, num_claims, num_chronic_conditions) |>
  drop_na() |>
  NULL  # replace NULL with scale()

# Print dimensions to verify
dim(clust_data)
```

```{r task1-check-scale}
# TODO: verify that all columns now have mean ≈ 0 and sd ≈ 1
apply(clust_data, 2, mean) |> round(4)
apply(clust_data, 2, sd)   |> round(4)
```

## Task 2: Elbow plot — choose k

```{r task2-elbow}
# TODO: compute WCSS for k = 1 to 10 using kmeans(..., nstart = 25)
# Store results in a vector called wcss
set.seed(602)
wcss <- sapply(1:10, function(k) NULL)  # replace NULL with kmeans call

# TODO: plot WCSS vs k using ggplot2
tibble(k = 1:10, wcss = wcss) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = k, y = wcss)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Elbow Method for Optimal k",
       x = "Number of clusters (k)", y = "Within-Cluster Sum of Squares") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r task2-choose-k}
# Based on the elbow plot, which k do you choose? Why?
# Answer (as a comment):
chosen_k <- NULL  # replace with your chosen integer
```

## Task 3: Fit k-means

```{r task3-fit}
set.seed(602)
# TODO: fit kmeans with chosen_k and nstart = 25
km <- NULL  # kmeans(clust_data, centers = chosen_k, nstart = 25)

# Print WCSS of the best run
cat("WCSS:", km$tot.withinss, "\n")
cat("Cluster sizes:", km$size, "\n")
```

```{r task3-silhouette}
# TODO: compute the silhouette score for your clustering
# sil <- silhouette(km$cluster, dist(clust_data))
# mean(sil[, "sil_width"])  -- report the mean silhouette score
# If the dataset is large, sample 5000 rows first for dist()
set.seed(42)
idx <- sample(nrow(clust_data), min(5000, nrow(clust_data)))
sil <- NULL  # silhouette(km$cluster[idx], dist(clust_data[idx, ]))
cat("Mean silhouette score:", round(mean(sil[, "sil_width"]), 3), "\n")
```

## Task 4: Profile clusters and assign labels

```{r task4-profile}
# TODO: add km$cluster as a column to the non-NA rows of health_data
# Then group_by(cluster) and summarise age, bmi, income, num_claims,
# num_chronic_conditions, and the proportion who smoke (mean(smoker))

health_clustered <- health_data |>
  drop_na(age, bmi, income, num_claims, num_chronic_conditions) |>
  mutate(cluster = factor(NULL))  # replace NULL with km$cluster

cluster_profile <- health_clustered |>
  group_by(cluster) |>
  summarise(
    n                = n(),
    avg_age          = NULL,  # mean(age)
    avg_bmi          = NULL,
    avg_income       = NULL,
    avg_claims       = NULL,
    pct_smoker       = NULL   # mean(smoker) * 100
  )

print(cluster_profile)
```
